---
title: "Neuroblastoma copy-number profiles"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE
)
lgr::get_logger("mlr3")$set_threshold("warn")
```

This case study learns penalties for real copy-number data and compares the four learners with an unsupervised penalty. The data are the neuroblastoma profiles used in Toby Hocking's [introduction to supervised changepoint detection](https://tdhock.github.io/change-tutorial/Supervised.html).

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(mlr3)
library(mlr3changepoint)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
```

## The data

Each profile is a tumour sample measured on a microarray. `profiles` has the log ratio of each probe, the logarithm of its copy number relative to a reference, so it rises with copy number but is not proportional to it, with its chromosome and its position in base pairs. `annotations` has the labels an expert drew: a genomic region from `min` to `max`, labelled `breakpoint` (at least one change) or `normal` (no change). Both names are in `penaltyLearning::change.labels`.

```{r}
data(neuroblastoma, package = "neuroblastoma")
profiles = data.table(neuroblastoma$profiles)
annotations = data.table(neuroblastoma$annotations)
profiles
annotations
```

## One sequence per chromosome

A changepoint problem is one chromosome of one profile, and only labelled chromosomes can be used for training. To keep the build fast, the task uses 200 of them, each with 20 to 300 probes.

```{r}
setkey(profiles, profile.id, chromosome, position)
setkey(annotations, profile.id, chromosome)
sizes = profiles[, .(n_probes = .N), by = .(profile.id, chromosome)]
labelled = unique(annotations[, .(profile.id, chromosome)])
problems = sizes[labelled, on = .(profile.id, chromosome), nomatch = NULL]
problems = problems[n_probes >= 20 & n_probes <= 300]
nrow(problems)
set.seed(1)
problems = problems[sort(sample(.N, 200L))]
```

The labels are in base pairs, but a `TaskCpt` counts positions along the signal. A change between probes $j$ and $j + 1$ sits at the midpoint of their positions, $m_j$. A region from `min` to `max` holds the changes with `min` $< m_j \le$ `max`. So `start` is the number of midpoints at or below `min`, and `end` is the number at or below `max`. `findInterval()` counts them. This mapping reproduces the target intervals in penaltyLearning's own processed neuroblastoma data exactly.

```{r}
signal = vector("list", nrow(problems))
label = vector("list", nrow(problems))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(problems))) {
  problem_id = problems[i, .(profile.id, chromosome)]
  probes = profiles[problem_id]
  regions = annotations[problem_id]
  mid = (probes$position[-nrow(probes)] + probes$position[-1L]) / 2
  signal[[i]] = probes$logratio
  label[[i]] = data.table(
    start = findInterval(regions$min, mid),
    end = findInterval(regions$max, mid),
    label = as.character(regions$annotation)
  )
}
task = TaskCpt$new(
  id = "neuroblastoma", backend = data.table(logratio = signal, label = label),
  target = "label", sequence = "logratio", label_type = "changepoint"
)
task
```

The row ids of the task are 1 to 200, in the order of `problems`.

## Benchmark

`Kmax = 5` lets each chromosome have up to five changes. The MMIT and MMIF learners join the benchmark when the mmit package is installed.

```{r}
kmax = 5L
learners = list(
  lrn("changepoint.intregrcv", Kmax = kmax),
  lrn("changepoint.xgboost.aft", Kmax = kmax)
)
if (requireNamespace("mmit", quietly = TRUE)) {
  learners = c(learners, lrns(c("changepoint.mmit", "changepoint.mmif"), Kmax = kmax))
}
```

The benchmark runs three-fold cross-validation with the same folds for every learner, scored by label error and AUC.

```{r}
measures = msrs(c("changepoint.label_error", "changepoint.auc"))
set.seed(1)
design = benchmark_grid(task, learners, rsmp("cv", folds = 3L))
bmr = benchmark(design)
scores = bmr$aggregate(measures)[, .(learner_id, changepoint.label_error, changepoint.auc)]
scores
```

## An unsupervised baseline

Without labels, a common choice is a BIC-style penalty, $\lambda = \log n$ for a sequence of $n$ probes, so $\log \lambda = \log \log n$. The loss here is the sum of squared residuals, so this matches BIC only when the noise variance is 1; for noise variance $\sigma^2$ BIC would use $\sigma^2 \log n$. It needs no training, so the baseline is a `PredictionCpt` built by hand for each test fold. A hand-made prediction records no `Kmax`, so `extra` gives it the same cap as the learners.

```{r}
n_probes = lengths(signal)
folds = design$resampling[[1L]]
baseline = list()
for (i in seq_len(folds$iters)) {
  rows = folds$test_set(i)
  prediction = PredictionCpt$new(
    task = task, row_ids = rows,
    response = log(log(n_probes[rows])),
    extra = list(Kmax = rep(kmax, length(rows)))
  )
  baseline[[i]] = as.data.table(as.list(prediction$score(measures, task = task)))
}
baseline = rbindlist(baseline)
scores = rbind(scores, data.table(learner_id = "BIC baseline", baseline[, lapply(.SD, mean)]))
scores
```

The baseline is scored on the same three test folds and averaged the same way. Its penalty depends only on the number of probes, while a learned penalty also follows the noise level of each profile, which the features measure. All four learners make fewer label errors than the baseline. The AUCs are all close to 1, so the baseline orders the sequences about as well as the learners do. Its penalties sit at the wrong level, which only the label error at the predicted penalties shows.

## ROC curve and profiles

The ROC curve below pools the cross-validated predictions of `changepoint.xgboost.aft`, the second learner in the design.

```{r, fig.width = 4, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "ROC curve of the cross-validated xgboost.aft predictions on the neuroblastoma task, with a dot at the predicted penalties."}
xgb_prediction = bmr$resample_result(2L)$prediction()
autoplot(xgb_prediction, task = task, type = "roc")
```

Four profiles with a `breakpoint` label show the changes those penalties select. `problems[shown]` gives their profile and chromosome.

```{r}
has_breakpoint = logical(length(label))
for (i in seq_along(label)) {
  has_breakpoint[i] = any(label[[i]]$label == "breakpoint")
}
shown = head(which(has_breakpoint), 4L)
problems[shown]
```

Each panel shows one chromosome, its labelled regions and dashed lines at the changes selected by the penalty predicted while it was in the test fold.

```{r, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Four chromosome profiles of log ratio against probe index, with shaded breakpoint and normal regions and dashed lines at the changes selected by the cross-validated xgboost.aft penalties."}
autoplot(xgb_prediction$filter(shown), task = task)
```
